recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Bio: Marty Leeds is a gematria researcher, author and preacher who founded The Gnostic Church and Academy of Lord Jesus Christ in 2022, where he serves as head teacher and spiritual leader. A working minister since 2011, he is the author of more than ten books, among them the Pi & The English Alphabet series, Scripture in the Stars, The Keys to the Tarot and Gnosticism Defined: The Tenets of The Order, built around a mathematical cipher he says is hidden beneath the English alphabet. His teaching centers on Prisca Theologia, the idea of a single wisdom underlying the world's religions, drawing together gematria, Kabbalah, astrology and comparative mythology. He streams weekly sermons free through the Gnostic Academy's YouTube and Rumble channels.
recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Name: Marty Leeds

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Gödel's Incompleteness and the Proof of God", "body": "Marty walks through Kurt Gödel's incompleteness theorem as a closed circle: anything you can draw a boundary around cannot explain itself without reference to something outside that boundary, whether it is a square on graph paper or the physical universe. He applies this to language itself, arguing that English cannot explain English and eventually you hit the edge of zero and nothing, the point where philosophy stops and religion begins. Since all meaning inside any closed system has to come from outside it, he treats the theorem as an accidental proof of a transcendent creator, joking that Gödel's own name literally spells God plus L."}, {"title": "Jesus as the Demiurge and the First Mind", "body": "Marty reframes the demiurge, insisting Jesus is the demiurge and that the word simply means worker, not a villain who trapped souls in an evil simulation. Drawing on the doctrine of emanations shared by Hinduism, Buddhism, and Christianity, he describes a first mind, or protogonos, rippling out of the zero point like the trunk of a tree, individuated consciousness before any others existed. That first being becomes the intermediary who helps every later branch stay in flow rather than decay, which is why Adam, Noah, and Christ repeat as incarnations of the same pattern, and why the earth itself deserves to be called sacred rather than cursed."}, {"title": "The Pole Star and the Guarded Poles", "body": "Building on astrotheology, Marty argues that the fixed Pole Star let ancient cultures find the still center of the heavens and, by extension, the North Pole on earth, since without a compass nobody would know which way was north. He turns that into a flat earth argument, claiming a compass at the South Pole would betray the model, which he says is reason enough for authorities to restrict access to the poles. He ties the constellations' hero journey stories to this hidden center, saying the elite suppress it because acknowledging a real middle to the realm would mean admitting a spiritual quest, and a real God, are equally real."}, {"title": "Ascension Cults and the Meaning of Transcendence", "body": "Marty draws a hard line between wanting to transcend and the ascension cults that promise an escape hatch through a chosen leader. Every such cult, he says, ends with followers being exploited, so his own rule as a minister is simply not to be followed but to point people back to God. He contrasts this with simulation theorists and detachment teachers who treat any remaining sense of self as a trap, arguing their actual goal is oblivion and annihilation, which he calls the path of self-hate. Real transcendence, in his framing, is graduation rather than escape, a good life can still be worth leaving once its lessons are complete."}, {"title": "Biofield Sessions and the Balance That Opens Heaven", "body": "In the exclusive back half, Chance describes his own biofield tuning work, where he sometimes encounters a stuck or fragmented ancestor carrying a pattern passed down to living relatives, and helping that fragment find wholeness can quietly heal the client too. He extends this into a theology of the afterlife where nothing is lost, God keeps a complete record of every life, and the real requirement for heaven is not a specific creed or ritual but a wholeness quotient, how balanced, moral, and honest a person becomes. Marty and Chance connect this to family lineage, how one person's healing can repair patterns reaching back through a family line."}]
